one_liner: LevelDB-based LSM KV server split into RDMA-linked compute and storage parts; beats LevelDB/RocksDB under skewed access.
what_it_does: Nova-LSM splits an LSM-tree store into LSM-tree components (LTCs: memtables, indexes, compaction coordination), a logging component (LogC) and storage components (StoCs: block storage and offloaded compaction), all connected over RDMA, so several LTCs can share the disk bandwidth of every StoC instead of each node using only its own disk. You use it as a network server (nova_server_main) with a custom socket protocol that has only GET, PUT and SCAN, driven by a Java YCSB binding, not as an embeddable library. The internal C++ DB class is a modified LevelDB API (no Write(WriteBatch), CompactRange commented out) that depends on process-global Nova config.
how_it_is_fast: It builds dynamic ranges (Dranges) inside each range, each with its own active memtables; writes are load-balanced across them, and Level0 SSTables from different Dranges do not overlap, so Level0-to-Level1 compaction runs in parallel and write stalls shrink. Hot keys stay in memory because memtables with fewer than 100 unique keys are merged rather than flushed, giving 65% less data written under skew. A lookup index sends each get to the single memtable or L0 SSTable that holds the latest version, and a range index lets scans skip stale versions of hot keys. SSTable blocks are scattered across rho StoCs, picked by power-of-d on disk-queue length, and compaction can be offloaded to StoCs.
when_to_use: You have a multi-node RDMA/InfiniBand cluster and want to reproduce or extend the SIGMOD 2021 disaggregated-LSM results. The repo ships CloudLab profiles, configs and experiment scripts.

Range-partitioned data with heavily skewed (Zipfian 0.99) access, where in a shared-nothing setup the node holding the hot range saturates its own disk. Pooling StoCs gave 9x or more over shared-nothing on a 1 TB, 10-node setup.
Write-heavy ingest with large memtable memory that stalls on Level0 compaction. With 10 StoCs, raising LTC memtable memory from 32 MB to 2 GB took W100 Uniform from 8.9K to 246K ops/s.
Scan-plus-write workloads on skewed keys (SW50 Zipfian), where LevelDB/RocksDB iterate every version of a hot key and Nova's range index skips them.
As a design reference for ideas you want to port into your own LSM engine: Dranges/Tranges, the memtable lookup index, power-of-d SSTable placement.
when_not_to_use: As an embedded RocksDB/LevelDB replacement inside an application process. It is a server with a static partition config, integer-only keys, and no atomic write batches (listed as future work in the paper).

Uniform-access, CPU-bound workloads. The paper reports a 15% range-index overhead on single-node SW50 Uniform and 20-30% lower throughput on CPU-intensive uniform workloads. On tmpfs it is 10-30% slower under Uniform, and RocksDB* (64 instances) beats it on SW50.

Clusters without RDMA, or with newer NICs. The setup scripts target mlx4 (ConnectX-3) packages. Open issue #3 reports an IBV_WC_RETRY_EXC_ERR segfault on ConnectX-5 CloudLab nodes, and open issue #2 asks how to run it on one local machine. Neither has an answer.

Anything that needs durability, deletes or ongoing support. Log replication is off by default (--log_record_mode=none), Delete does not write a tombstone, and the project has no releases or tags and no activity since 2021.

integration.form: static lib + server binary (CMake builds libleveldb plus nova_server_main); used in practice as a standalone server
integration.dependencies: libibverbs (RDMA verbs; linked unconditionally), libevent, gflags (static .a required), fmt (script installs 6.1.2 from source), pthreads; optional crc32c and snappy. Clients use the separate Java NovaLSM-YCSB-Client binding.
integration.min_toolchain: C++11 (-std=c++11), CMake 3.9+; compiler hard-coded to /usr/bin/g++, version not documented
integration.platforms: Linux only (tested on CloudLab R320 and c6220 x86-64 nodes); multi-node mode needs an RDMA NIC (scripts load mlx4/ConnectX-3 drivers)
integration.thread_safety: db.h keeps LevelDB's statement that a DB is safe for concurrent access from multiple threads. The server runs hundreds of worker threads per LTC. The paper says scans that span two ranges run at read-committed isolation.

gotchas: Keys must be decimal-integer strings. The comparator (YCSBKeyComparator) and the Drange code parse keys with str_to_int. The server routes keys by numeric range from a static config file and asserts the key is within it. The lookup index is a dense array with one 4-byte slot for every integer in [lower_key, upper_key), allocated when the DB opens.

Delete is not a real delete. DB::Delete calls WriteMemTablePool(key, Slice()), and every write path adds kTypeValue, so a deleted key reads back as an empty value rather than NotFound. The socket protocol has no DELETE at all.

The paper's features are off by default. --enable_lookup_index, --enable_range_index and --enable_subrange all default to false, and logging defaults to none. The paper's comparison ran with logging disabled for every system. A failed Put hits NOVA_ASSERT and aborts the server.

The default build is unoptimized: CMakeLists sets -g with no -O level and no CMAKE_BUILD_TYPE, and also builds -pg profiling binaries. nova_server_main multiplies --max_stoc_file_size_mb by 1024 only once; open issue #3 asks whether that is a bug, with no answer.
pick_this_over_siblings_when: Pick it only when the bottleneck is one node's disk under skewed, range-partitioned load and you have an RDMA cluster to pool disks across nodes. Otherwise KVell, SplinterDB, PebblesDB, MatrixKV and Titan are far easier single-node engines to adopt (Titan loads as a RocksDB plugin; MatrixKV attacks the same write-stall problem with an NVM tier instead of Dranges).
verified_claims_summary: With YCSB 1 KB records on CloudLab c6220 nodes (2x Xeon E5-2650v2, 64 GB, one 1 TB HDD, 56 Gbps InfiniBand), logging off for all systems and compiler and RocksDB version unstated, Nova-LSM beat LevelDB/RocksDB by 2.3x to 18x under Zipfian access on a 2 TB, 10-node database, and on one node reached 105x over a single LevelDB instance on SW50 Zipfian but only about 1.4x over 64-instance RocksDB*. Under Uniform access throughput was roughly equal or lower, and the RocksDB/LevelDB wrapper binaries (rocksdb_main, leveldb_main) are not in the repo, whose checked-in RocksDB script sets block_cache_mb=0.
status_note: Abandoned research prototype (last master commit 2021-06-20, a contributed db_bench branch merged 2021-12-15, no releases, two open issues unanswered) under BSD-3-Clause, so it can legally be copied, but it is tied to CloudLab/mlx4 scripts and is not realistically usable as a dependency.
